item.description:
At our annual Google for Brazil event, we shared updates on how we're bringing new AI tools and features to Brazil:
📍 Ask Maps is coming to Brazil in Portuguese, so you can get your questions answered conversationally with a customized map. ⚡ We're expanding Gemini in Chrome to Brazil. 📚 Students can soon study for the ENEM exam with a dedicated experience on Gemini and NotebookLM. 📅 With new agentic capabilities on AI Mode in Search, we're helping people book and manage restaurant reservations through a conversational experience.
We're also investing in providing AI training to more Brazilians by expanding the Experience AI program through a new Google.org grant, offering new scholarships for Google Career Certificates and more.
Learn more about all the announcements from Google for Brazil → https://goo.gle/4exXGg9

item.description:
Still using your dog’s name and your birth year as your corporate password? Don’t be your IT department’s worst nightmare. By switching to a passkey — if your organization has opted in — you’ll be able to sign-in to your Google accounts securely using just a fingerprint, face scan or screen lock.
For National Fishing Week, we’re sharing some pro tips about passkeys to help you stay safe from phishing scams and keep your sign-in secure 🎣
Plus, you can learn more about other key Google tools you can take advantage of so you don’t lose access. https://goo.gle/4vZ5DRF

item.title: 20 years ago, Google Translate started as a small experiment to help people learn, speak and connect more deeply than ever before. 🌏 💬 Today we'...
item.description:
20 years ago, Google Translate started as a small experiment to help people learn, speak and connect more deeply than ever before. 🌏 💬
Today we're taking a big step forward with Gemini 3.5 Live Translate — our latest audio model for live, speech-to-speech translation across 70+ languages.
By translating continuously as you speak, Gemini 3.5 Live Translate generates smooth, natural-sounding speech without pauses. This helps ensure that your message — and your personal delivery — doesn't get lost in translation, no matter the language.
Gemini 3.5 Live Translate brings live, natural speech translation to everyone globally in Google Translate on Android and iOS and to developers in public preview via the Gemini Live API and Google AI Studio.
Soon, Google Meet will use Gemini 3.5 Live Translate for Speech Translation. We’re launching this update in private preview for select business Google Workspace customers starting this month, followed by a broader rollout later this year.
Learn more → goo.gle/4xjMdZ1

item.title: It takes more than just engineers to build the future of AI — it also takes people who can turn complexity into a clear strategy. Tara, Executive Bus...
item.description:
It takes more than just engineers to build the future of AI — it also takes people who can turn complexity into a clear strategy. Tara, Executive Business Partner in the Cloud Applied AI team, is that reliable anchor. While her team builds the future of Google Cloud, Tara ensures leadership stays focused on technical breakthroughs. “AAI (Applied AI) is very fast-moving with shifting priorities,” she explains. “As the ‘right-hand’ to the VP of Eng, my job is to ensure that she can focus on technical breakthroughs while I manage the ‘business of the business’.”
Beyond her core work, Tara’s involvement with GAIN (Google Aboriginal and Indigenous Network) helps bridge the gap between innovation and local culture — like naming meeting rooms using Indigenous languages and concepts. “GAIN Canada coordinates with local Elders and language speakers to ensure that the chosen names are appropriate, respectful and used with permission,” she explains.
If you’re ready to bring your own strategy to the world of AI, explore our open roles → https://goo.gle/48mIFui

item.title: Since 2025, Google has provided funding to help the electrical training ALLIANCE (etA) train thousands of electrical workers and the Manufacturing Ins...
item.description:
Since 2025, Google has provided funding to help the electrical training ALLIANCE (etA) train thousands of electrical workers and the Manufacturing Institute get thousands of workers essential AI skills. To help further close the workforce gap, we’re now expanding our total skilled trades support to $50 million to help prepare more than 300,000 American workers for the jobs of tomorrow. Learn more from Ruth Porat ⬇️ Today Google announced a meaningful expansion of our skilled trades training program, including funding for training experts whose work supports 14 labor unions and 4 trade associations across welders, pipefitters, sheet metal workers, electricians, and more. The goal of the effort is to ensure workers have the state-of-the-art skills and accreditation to pursue a skilled trades career, no matter where they want to work. We launched this effort over a year ago with the electrical training ALLIANCE (etA), and I am proud that with this expansion, Google will enable paths to high-paying careers for more than 300,000 American workers across more than 20 states.
It has been inspiring to meet trainees in the program and hear their excitement about the valuable careers this enables. Building the physical infrastructure for America’s future requires significantly increasing the pipeline of skilled tradespeople across the country – a challenge that can only be addressed with collective action across the private sector, civil society, and government. Google is proud to partner with these exceptional training experts and trade organizations. Learn more: https://lnkd.in/eRZUXwQj
